references.text: John 14:13 contains the immediately preceding verse that expands on the promise of prayer in Jesus' name, where Jesus says: 'Whatever you ask in my name, I will do it, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son.' This creates a direct contextual and theological link to verse 14.

John 15:16 repeats the promise of prayer in Jesus' name with almost identical wording: 'It is not you who chose me, but I who chose you... and whatever you ask the Father in my name, he will give it to you.' This is a direct parallel within the same authorship and theme.

John 16:23-24 confirms and elaborates on the principle of praying in Jesus' name: 'On that day you will not ask me anything. Truly, truly, I say to you: Whatever you ask the Father in my name, he will give it to you.' This is the third and final direct statement about this specific promise in the Gospel of John.

John 14:12 sets the stage for the promise in verse 14 by linking acts of faith to Jesus' name: 'Truly, truly, I say to you: Whoever believes in me will also do the works that I do, and they will do even greater works than these.' This explains 'why' Jesus will do what they ask.

John 16:26 confirms that the Father himself answers prayers offered in Jesus' name: 'On that day you will ask in my name. I do not say to you that I will ask the Father on your behalf.' This underscores the direct access to the Father through the name, which is the core of verse 14.
